title: KDP Interior Bleed Error: "Bleed" vs "No Bleed" Doesn't Match Your PDF | SparkPrep
h1: How to fix a KDP interior that doesn't match your bleed setting
description: KDP flags your manuscript because its page size doesn't match the bleed setting you picked. Learn the right page size with and without bleed, and fix it quickly.
lead: When you set up a paperback, KDP asks "Bleed" or "No bleed". Your PDF's page size has to match the answer exactly.
error: Your manuscript's page size doesn't match the trim size and bleed settings you selected
errorNote: Paraphrased. Each printer words this a little differently.
why:
No bleed means nothing on your pages touches the edge, so each PDF page is exactly your trim size (for example 6" x 9").

Bleed means pictures or color run off the edge, so each page must be bigger: 0.125" wider and 0.25" taller (6.125" x 9.25" for a 6" x 9" book). If you pick bleed but upload trim-size pages, or the other way round, KDP flags it, or your pictures end up with white edges.
manual: Decide: does anything on your pages need to touch the edge? If yes, you need bleed. If no, choose no bleed.
Open your manuscript and set the page size to match: trim size for no bleed, or trim + 0.125" wide and + 0.25" tall for bleed.
For bleed, stretch edge-to-edge pictures out to the new page edge; keep text inside the margins.
Re-export as a PDF and make sure the KDP setup (Bleed / No bleed) matches what you built.
Re-upload it and wait for the review again (KDP says a review can take up to 72 hours).

cta.text: SparkPrep checks every page's size against your trim and bleed choice and resizes the pages for you, in minutes.

faq.q: What size should a 6x9 interior PDF be with bleed?
faq.a: 6.125" x 9.25". Without bleed it's exactly 6" x 9".

faq.q: Do I need bleed for a novel?
faq.a: Usually not. You only need bleed when pictures, color blocks or shapes run off the edge of the page.
